transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-18
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~34 minutes
Attendees: Lila Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Emily Chen (North Bay CTO), Ravi Patel (North Bay Head of ML), Sofia Gomez (Product)

Summary (auto-generated, may have errors):
Quick model catalog walkthrough focused on selecting open models for clinical note summarization and triage. Discussed benchmarks (latency, tokens/sec), compatibility across quantization levels and CPU/GPU runtimes, and deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC). Customer interested in end-to-end POC and wants security docs and a compatibility matrix.

Topics: model catalog, benchmarks, compat matrix, deployment mode, security/SOC2, KV cache behavior, latency vs cost tradeoffs.

00:00 Lila: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick roll call, can you hear me okay?
00:04 Emily: Yeah good here, thanks.
00:07 Ravi: Yep, can hear you.
00:10 Sofia: All good.
00:15 Lila: Great. So today Marco and I are gonna run through our model catalog, show how you can pick open models, look at our benchmark pages, and then go into compatibility matrices - basically help you evaluate which models make sense for your clinical summarization workload.
00:28 Marco: Just to set expectations, we'll show hosted flow, then dedicated options and finally the private deployment notes. We'll point out where performance curves change with sequence length and quantization.
00:36 Emily: Sounds perfect - our main ask is cost + latency tradeoff for the triage/summary pipeline, and whether we can ship with hosted initially then move to private later.
00:48 Lila: Totally. Quick question on success criteria - what does a win look like for you in the POC?
00:53 Ravi: For ML, it's generating accurate summaries with under 200ms p95 for short notes (~256 tokens) and under 1s for longer notes (~1k tokens) when possible; cost per 1k tokens should be competitive vs self-hosting numbers we have.
01:06 Sofia: From product, we want consistent latency, and the outputs shouldn't hallucinate diagnoses - we need safety/QA hooks.
01:14 Lila: Good - we'll keep those front-and-center.

01:30 Marco: Jumping into the catalog - if you look at the page (shared in chat: https://redwood.ai/model-catalog) you'll see filters: topology (decoder, encoder-decoder), size, license, and performance profiles. For open models we curate quantized variants too - e.g., LlamaX-7B q4_0 and q8_0 tested.
01:48 Ravi: Quick Q: when you say q4_0 does that mean 4-bit quantization with no fine-tuning?
01:52 Marco: Right, it's post-training static quant. It preserves most of the quality for generation tasks in our tests; we show a delta column with Rouge/BLEU style metrics per workload. Sometimes the quality hit is minimal for summarization.
02:05 Emily: How reliable are those deltas? Our prompts are clinical and may be sensitive - small quality drops are bad.
02:12 Marco: Understood. We provide benchmark artifacts - per-model evaluation on custom prompt sets is recommended. For clinical specifically, we suggest running a small eval set (50-200 examples) under the POC. We'll help run that vs our precomputed benchmarks.
02:25 Ravi: Makes sense. Can you show the compatibility matrix?

02:30 Marco: Sure - opening the matrix (shared link in chat: https://redwood.ai/compat-matrix). This shows model architecture vs supported runtimes, quant profiles, and recommended hardware. Note that some open models are not supported on our TPU backends, but are on GPU and CPU. The matrix also flags KV cache behavior - some models need special handling for long-context streaming.
02:52 Sofia: I saw a note about KV cache - what's the practical impact for streaming clinical notes?
03:00 Marco: Two parts: prefix caching for repeated prompts speeds up cold start. For long-context (1k+ tokens) we rely on optimized KV cache with offload to host RAM for some quantized kernels; that keeps throughput good but can add small latency jitter. We surface that in the per-model bench.
03:15 Ravi: Does offload mean we hit CPU memory bandwidth? Any degradation?
03:19 Marco: Possibly; on high concurrency the host memory path can be a bottleneck. For P95-sensitive use cases we recommend dedicated pools or pinning to GPUs with larger VRAM to avoid offload. We'll show the numbers.

03:40 Lila: Here's a benchmark slide - we ran summarization suite A across several open models. The key cols: p50/p95 latency at sequence lengths 256/1024, tokens/sec, and relative token cost.
03:53 Emily: I notice one model has good latency but high cost - what's driving that?
03:57 Marco: Often it's a combination of model size and inability to quantize effectively. Some architectures don't quantize down well without quality loss, so you pay for larger compute. Also batching efficiency on some kernels is lower.
04:12 Ravi: Any head-to-head with Anthropic or OpenAI in your public bench?
04:17 Lila: We have apples-to-oranges notes; direct head-to-heads are tricky because endpoints differ. We do include external provider comparisons for latency/cost at similar latency SLOs but we recommend you run the exact prompts.
04:28 Sofia: Security question - for hosted, what is data retention? We can't have PHI persist beyond 30 days without agreements.
04:35 Lila: Hosted by default has short retention windows but for PHI we recommend Private deployment or Dedicated with data isolation; we also have retention controls and can set logs to be scrubbed. We'll send the security pack and SOC2 docs.
04:47 Emily: Good. Are you SOC2 Type II?
04:50 Lila: Yes, SOC2 Type II. We'll attach the cert.

05:05 Marco: Back to models - here's an example: MedMini-3B (open license) had p95 420ms at 256 tokens on A100, q4_0 had 10% lower latency and ~2-3% drop in ROUGE on our summary set. For longer contexts, the delta increases slightly.
05:24 Ravi: Could you quantify the hallucination rate difference?
05:27 Marco: We measure a safety score via hallucination checks - the difference was ~1.2% extra hallucination instances at q4_0 vs fp16 on that dataset. But again that's dataset dependent.
05:38 Emily: Okay that's useful - we'll want to test on our anonymized notes.

06:00 Marco: Also note compatibility with Redwood Optimize: our suggestions engine will recommend when to quantize vs when to keep fp16 based on average seq length and traffic patterns. It can automatically propose batching and cache settings to hit a target p95 or cost.
06:18 Sofia: Can Optimize integrate with our observability stack? We use Datadog and internal traces.
06:22 Marco: Yes - we surface per-route metrics and can forward traces via OTLP/Datadog integrations. You'll see token-level cost and latency breakdowns.

06:40 Ravi: For the POC, we'd like to run a benchmark on our sample 500-record set. How much runway do you need to run that?
06:46 Lila: If you can upload a sanitized sample set and give read access or drop in S3 link, we can run the bench in ~48 hours. Marco will need the prompts and expected labels.
06:56 Marco: Also we'll need to know concurrency expectations and whether to test hosted vs dedicated. We usually run both to show delta.
07:05 Ravi: Concurrency initially small - 10-20 QPS peak, moving to few hundred in prod.
07:10 Marco: Ok, we'll tune for that. For 10-20 QPS, batching is moderate; dedicated may not be necessary initially.

07:28 Emily: About private deployment - what's required on our side?
07:32 Lila: For VPC/private you run a small agent, we give a control plane that can be hosted but with private networking. For on-prem we provide an air-gapped package. You'll need approved KMS/HSM for keys if you want customer-managed keys.
07:46 Emily: Any differences in model catalog for private vs hosted?
07:49 Marco: Mostly parity; some experimental kernels we only ship in hosted initially but core open models and quant profiles are identical. There may be delays for brand-new custom kernels.

08:05 Sofia: Is there an SLA for dedicated customers?
08:08 Lila: Yes, Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we can surface the exact numbers in the contract.

08:20 Marco: Small demo - I'll show live selection flow: filter to license=MIT/Apache, size < 8B, task=summarization. You get a shortlist; clicking a model surfaces precomputed bench and links to artifacts. (screen share)
08:38 Marco: Here we click MedMini-3B, open the bench tab - you'll see p50/p95, tokens/sec, cost-estimate at current retail GPU pricing, and compatibility matrix rows. There's also a link "run on sample" which will let you run your uploaded prompt set against the model.
08:53 Ravi: Is that sandboxed? We don't want data to persist.
08:56 Marco: Sandbox run respects your retention policy and can be configured to not persist any results; we can also stream outputs directly to your S3 target.
09:06 Emily: You mentioned function/tool calling earlier for structured outputs - can that help reduce hallucinations?
09:11 Marco: Yes, schema enforcement + tool-calling reduces free-text drift. For structured clinical output we recommend enforced schemas and validators in the pipeline.

09:28 Lila: Quick note on pricing: hosted per-token plus embedding/compute; Dedicated is committed monthly with predictable unit economics which can be cheaper at scale. We'll send pricing tiers.
09:39 Sofia: Do you have references in healthcare?
09:42 Lila: We have a few health-tech customers (we'll anonymize), and we'll share case studies where they moved from hosted to dedicated.

09:55 Marco: One more technical - quantization profiles: we support q4_0, q8_0, q2_mixed in some cases. q2_mixed is aggressive and not recommended for summarization unless you validate on your prompts. The compatibility matrix flags which models pass a quality threshold at each quant.
10:14 Ravi: If we want to keep fp16 but lower cost, do you have hybrid approaches?
10:18 Marco: Yes: we do routing by policy - low-latency small requests hit smaller fp16 models; large batch jobs hit larger models with batching. Also prefix caching helps a lot on repeated prompts. Optimize can suggest routes automatically.

10:40 Emily: Ok, let's recap next steps.
10:44 Lila: Recap: we'll send the model catalog deck + security pack (SOC2, certs), Marco will share compatibility matrix and notes on KV cache/quantization, we'll run a POC bench on your sanitized 500-record set once you share it, and we'll propose dates for POC kickoff.
10:59 Ravi: Sounds good. Who owns the POC run?
11:02 Marco: We'll run and co-own the bench; you'll provide data and acceptance criteria.
11:07 Sofia: Timeline wise, if we get data by 24th, a 48h run plus analysis is fine - POC kickoff late March works.
11:15 Lila: Great, we'll aim for that. Any final Qs?
11:20 Emily: One more - legal: terms around data handling we'd need in an addendum.
11:24 Lila: Yes we'll loop in legal and include a DPA addendum.
11:28 Ravi: Thanks everyone.
11:30 Lila: Thanks - we'll follow up with links and owner list.
